title: Guardian experiment runner and Bayesian safeguards for model A/Bing
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a first-class A/B testing controller (Guardian) in the Console + runtime that supports: experiment creation (variants, cohorts, metrics), exposure budgets and per-cohort caps, shadow traffic validation, Bayesian sequential checks for early stopping, and automated rollback policies. Focus is to enable product teams to run statistically-sound experiments with safety budgets and deterministic auto-rollback while minimizing latency and KV-cache fragmentation in the serving runtime.
background: Current model rollout tooling supports simple traffic splits and manual canaries but lacks sequential-stat checks and tight exposure controls required by enterprise customers.
Teams often run shadow traffic experiments in an ad-hoc manner; we need a unified flow that ties shadow validations to eligibility gates and auto-rollback triggers.
We must balance statistical power, exposure risk, and runtime efficiency (batching/KV cache locality).
goals: Expose a Console flow to define experiments with: primary and variant models, metric definitions (primary/guards), cohorts, and exposure budgets.
Implement Bayesian sequential testing that evaluates win/loss/continue probabilities at configurable intervals.
Provide shadow traffic mode with sampled validation pipelines and delayed metric collection for offline quality checks.
Add an auto-rollback engine that executes safe rollbacks when statistical/operational thresholds are violated.
Ensure minimal runtime overhead: sampling + shadow routing should not increase p95 latency beyond 5% for production classes.
acceptance_criteria: Console has an Experiment Create page that lets user select models, cohorts, exposure schedule, primary metric and guard metrics.
Experiments support: ramp schedules (time-based), exposure budgets, per-cohort caps, and shadow validation toggles.
The Guardian engine runs Bayesian sequential checks every evaluation window and outputs: continue/win/fail probabilities to Console and logs.
Auto-rollback rules can be defined (statistical threshold + operational threshold e.g., error rate > X) and successfully revert traffic when triggered in staging.
Shadow mode can mirror 1% of prod traffic to variant, collect responses, and surface quality deltas in an experiment dashboard within 30 minutes of data arrival.
End-to-end integration tests exist for a canary rollout -> detect regression -> auto-rollback scenario in a dedicated staging environment.
design_considerations: Statistical approach: choose Bayesian sequential testing (posterior probability that variant is better by delta) to enable adaptive stopping with clear priors and less multiple-testing complexity.
Latency concerns: prefer sampling+asynchronous shadow validation rather than synchronous mirroring to avoid increasing p95. Implement off-path validation pipeline writing to a metrics topic.
KV cache impact: avoid fragmenting KV caches by limiting cohort routing to production model variants with compatible kv-cache key formats; document fallback when cache miss rate increases.
Exposure safety: default exposure budgets to conservative values for new experiments (max 5% total exposure for first 24 hours), require explicit PM approval to raise budgets.
Operational signals: combine statistical signals with operational ones (e.g., error rate, latency spike, hallucination rate) to avoid false positives driven by small sample anomalies.
technical_notes: Runtime will surface per-request metadata for cohort and experiment id so we can attribute metrics in observability pipeline (tracing + counters).
Guardian controller will run in Console back-end and push routing changes via Control Plane API; fallbacks are enforced in runtime so rollback can happen without Console availability.
Evaluation windows default to 60 mins but are configurable; we use incremental posterior updates to avoid reprocessing raw events each check.
We will serialize experiment configs to a compact proto stored in the routing cache for fast lookup during request routing.

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: premature rollbacks due to noisy signals. Mitigation: require combined statistical + operational threshold and minimum sample size before rollback executes.
Risk: increased latency from synchronous shadow mirroring. Mitigation: use sampled async shadow pipeline and off-path validation jobs.
Risk: KV cache fragmentation when routing by cohort. Mitigation: group cohorts with identical cache key prefix heuristics and cap cohort velocity.
Risk: customers misconfigure exposure budgets. Mitigation: add conservative defaults, contextual warnings in Console, and require approval for >10% exposures.

qa_plan: Unit tests for Bayesian posterior calculation with synthetic priors.
Integration tests: Console -> Control Plane -> Runtime routing updates and rollback path.
Staging scenario: inject regression in variant and verify detection and rollback within configured SLO.
Load test: ensure p95 latency increase <5% with 1% async shadowing enabled.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Early access to internal teams, conservative budgets, manual review of first 10 experiments.
Phase 2: Gradual enable for PLG users with default budgets and opt-in shadow validation.
Phase 3: Enterprise rollout with RBAC and approval workflow for exposures >10%.
notes: Consider future: gated ensemble where multiple small variants are run and an ensemble controller picks best at inference time (long-term).
We should connect eval corpus failures to experiment guards so we can have deterministic rollback on known safety regression patterns.
Follow-up: add a simulation mode in Console that predicts time-to-detect given expected traffic and effect size.
